solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Case of feed swallowed in birds' craws

indicators.note: something swallowed in a bird ends up inside it, so the trimmed piece goes within the birds' letters

parts.note: gulls are seabirds

indicators.note: only the case, the outer shell, of the word for feed is kept, its middle letter dropped

parts.note: to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes food going down into the crops of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' acts on a synonym of feed, not on the printed word: only its outer shell survives, which the seabirds then swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A craw is a bird's crop or throat passage, the same tube as an oesophagus or food pipe.

parts.note: reads like a question about a city, but capital here means money: the old Dutch currency before the euro

explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch currency until the euro replaced it in 2002 was this coin, so it was the country's money, its capital.

clue.text: Runs edge of axe in cuts

indicators.note: the first letter of axe is placed inside the word for cuts

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its first letter here, taken from axe

explanation.surface: A woodsman's axe blade wears down as it hacks away.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides, so runs is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Ale without a head? That is unnatural

indicators.note: a pint without a head loses its froth; here the word for ale loses its first letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that a flat pint with no froth is just wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER without its head leaves EER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird and uncanny, beyond the natural order, is spooky in this way.

clue.text: More biting following small first course

indicators.note: the word for more biting comes after the abbreviation for small

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
tarter means sharper or more biting in taste or tone

explanation.surface: A menu note: something sharper comes after a small opening dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening dish of a meal is the appetiser served before the main.

indicators.note: signals that the word for sailor is heard, not spelt, and replaced by a sound-alike

parts.note: an old salt is a veteran sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman, so they say, has turned rude.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive in military use is an attack, a noun meaning a strike against the enemy.

clue.text: Adult, bored, taking time to get dressed

parts.note: A is the old film-classification letter for adult

indicators.note: the word for bored takes the time abbreviation into itself

parts.note: tired means weary or bored

explanation.surface: A weary grown-up takes their time getting ready to go out.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothed and dressed are synonyms, both describing someone who has put on clothes.

clue.text: These cut with ease separating ends of roses

indicators.note: pulling the letters of the two words apart lets them be rebuilt in another order
the ends of roses are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Garden tools that snip through rose stems effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separating' scrambles CUT and EASE into SECATEU; 'ends of' roses gives R and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue word refers back to the garden tools described, a pair of pruning shears that cut with ease.

indicators.note: the two words grab the answer between them, holding its letters in their run

explanation.surface: A cad hung around and seized a housemaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is one example of a servant or subordinate, a junior person working under others.

indicators.note: the leader of terrorist is its first letter

parts.note: a reason is a cause or motive

explanation.surface: A news line on the motive behind a terror chief's plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country by trying to overthrow it is subversion of the state.

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A vagrant heads off into the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' looks like part of the tramp's journey, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading figure is a prominent or significant one, so the adjectives match.

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel or bounder

indicators.note: turning the abbreviation round reads it backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: A rogue, for instance, turns tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' here is the verb, to scrounge, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum a cigarette is to scrounge or beg one, the same sense as sponging.

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors, police officers
a ball shot into the net is sent there

explanation.surface: Officers open fire during a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreement voiced against authority is objection, which is what protest means.

definitions.meaning: counters as a verb: replies sharply or ripostes
glass flasks with long bent necks used for distilling in a lab

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: quick comebacks in argument, and the necked glass vessels chemists distil in.

clue.text: Left-winger touring English bay Queen came round

indicators.note: the left-winger's word travels around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a red is a communist or socialist
a cove is a small bay
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A socialist tours a coastal inlet and the monarch regains consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who came round after fainting has regained consciousness, healed and back to normal.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the other comes first

parts.note: an auto is a car
the US is an example of a country or state

explanation.surface: America backs a car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory in the surface, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink or red flower, popular in buttonholes, is a garden bloom of the pink family.

clue.text: Unfortunately I've sublet part of house

indicators.note: things gone wrong are disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant regrets subletting a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance hall or lobby is a room in a home, the area just inside the front door.

clue.text: Aggravation of member blowing top for coalition

indicators.note: losing one's top here means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling that aggravates a toe or foot, a limb or member

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper over a nuisance in the alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' sounds like losing one's temper; it drops the B of BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of parties or states joined together is a coalition.

indicators.note: the duke's letter goes inside the word for battles

parts.note: wars are battles or conflicts

explanation.surface: Accusations levelled at an aristocrat over his campaigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests accusations; here it means young people in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Minors placed under a guardian's protection are that guardian's charges.

clue.text: Bird's cry around a great void

indicators.note: the word for cry goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to wail is to cry loudly

indicators.note: a void word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A bird's call echoes round an immense empty space.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird known for constantly wagging its long tail.

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound or crooked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wise caution about looking a suspect gift horse in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning ahead with care is a form of foresight; the two words are near synonyms.

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer inside their run of letters

explanation.surface: A sleepy golfer wakes up with a club in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' looks like a golf club in this surface; it is used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Containing or relating to iron is what this chemistry adjective means, from Latin ferrum.

clue.text: Alleged grass will get placed inside

indicators.note: the word for placed goes inside the word for grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
put means placed

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: lawn seed will be sown indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported or believed to be so without proof, as in the reputed father, is alleged.

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so this is the verb to harry, to pester

indicators.note: the word for wrong holds the other word within it

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: A man named Harry is wrong to hold someone's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, close in sense to pestering or plaguing someone.

indicators.note: the word for slacker comes after the letter from midnight

parts.note: the middle of night is its central letter
lazier means more slack or idle

explanation.surface: A tradesman goes idle after twelve at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the middle of 'night', its letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fits glass into windows is a skilled tradesman.

indicators.note: a word's tail is its final letter, taken from sheep's

parts.note: latter means last of two, the final one

explanation.surface: Lamb's tail served before the final course.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat serving plate is a dish.

indicators.note: the word for mum is embraced, held inside the word for when

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
ma is a word for mum

explanation.surface: A family gathers whenever mother gets a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather or accumulate is to collect things together.

indicators.note: in a down clue the topping piece sits above the rest
the central letter of custard is picked

parts.note: ripe means fully developed or mature

explanation.surface: Custard topping a dish of mature rhubarb, a pudding description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhubarb' is not the stewed fruit but slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or rubbish talk, a synonym for drivel.

parts.note: François Hollande was a French president, so a farewell said to him would be in French

explanation.definitionFit: This is the French word for goodbye, literally to God, used for a final parting.

clue.text: A corset is removed in bar

indicators.note: the letters are moved from where they stand into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone takes off their corset in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to exclude or shut them out, as does shunning them socially.

clue.text: Agrees to go round pub for birds

indicators.note: the word for agrees goes round the pub's word

parts.note: lets means allows or agrees to
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone consents to buy a round at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: These small finches are songbirds.

clue.text: Fool possibly stranded initially in wasteland

indicators.note: the initial letter is placed in the word for wasteland

parts.note: a desert is barren wasteland

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of stranded is used

explanation.surface: A clown is left stranded in a barren desert.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is also a creamy fruit pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool, whipped cream with fruit, is one example of a pudding course.
